content.title: Fonts: embedded defaults, opt-in discovery
content.lede: Every PDF can use the bundled Liberation Sans, Serif, and Mono families plus a DejaVu Sans fallback, with no font scanning at all. Runes above U+00FF switch to a Type0/CID path, and OpenType shaping applies only as far as the face tables and the pure-Go engine allow.

items.title: Bundled: Liberation plus DejaVu
items.body: Every conversion can use Liberation Sans, Liberation Serif, and Liberation Mono (Regular / Bold / Italic / BoldItalic) plus DejaVu Sans Regular+Bold as the Unicode fallback. Faces are embedded from `internal/pdf/assets` and parsed lazily by `pdf.LoadDefaultFaces`; Latin-1 text uses a simple TrueType subset with WinAnsi-style single-byte codes.

items.title: Opt-in: discovered faces
items.body: `--font-path DIR` scans `DIR` plus two levels of subdirectories (`pdf.ScanFontDirs`, `fontScanMaxDepth = 2`) for `.ttf` and `.otf` files and is repeatable. `--use-system-fonts` also scans common OS font directories such as `/usr/share/fonts` while skipping proprietary Windows and corefont trees.

items.title: Matching and fallback
items.body: `pdf.FaceSet.ResolveFamily` maps common names and generics onto bundled faces: `serif` / `georgia` / `times` -> Liberation Serif; `monospace` / `courier` / `consolas` -> Liberation Mono; `sans-serif` / `arial` / `helvetica` -> Liberation Sans; `system-ui` / `DejaVu Sans` -> bundled DejaVu. Names outside the table resolve against the opt-in registry first, then fall through the author's comma stack to Liberation Sans.

items.title: CJK readiness
items.body: Han, kana, and Hangul render when a capable TTF is on the font path, for example `fonts-noto-cjk`. Production Hangul needs a Hangul-capable TTF on `--font-path`; the tiny OFL subset `NotoSansKR-HangulSubset.ttf` in `testdata/fonts` exists for CI and the fixture-27 smoke test only, not as a production CJK face.

content.heading: Font flags and discovery behavior
rows: Scan `DIR` plus two levels of subdirectories for `.ttf` / `.otf`; repeatable (`pdf.ScanFontDirs`, `fontScanMaxDepth = 2`)
Also scan common OS font directories (e.g. `/usr/share/fonts`); skips proprietary Windows/corefont trees
Bundled mapping covers common names and generics (`pdf.FaceSet.ResolveFamily`); other names resolve named via the opt-in registry, then fall through the comma stack to Liberation Sans

Missing IPA / uncommon Unicode glyphs walk CSS family (registry, then bundled) -> Liberation weight/style -> bundled DejaVu -> any opt-in registry face that covers the codepoint (`pdf.Registry.FindWithGlyph`, prefers DejaVu/Noto names)
Bundled Liberation Sans / Serif / Mono (R/B/I/BI) and DejaVu Sans Regular+Bold available; Latin-1 uses a simple TrueType subset with WinAnsi-style single-byte codes

content.heading: CJK / Hangul with --font-path
content.code:
gowkhtmltopdf --font-path /usr/share/fonts/truetype/droid \
  --font-path testdata/fonts \
  fixture-27-cjk-fontpath.html out.pdf
# Production Hangul: fonts-noto-cjk or any Hangul-capable TTF on --font-path
#   --font-path /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto
# testdata/fonts/NotoSansKR-HangulSubset.ttf is a tiny OFL subset for CI
# and the fixture-27 smoke test only, not a full CJK face.

sections.heading: Type0 / CID for code points above U+00FF
sections.body: When a text run contains code points above U+00FF (after punctuation folding), the writer switches that run onto a Type0 / CIDFontType2 sibling resource with Identity-H encoding and Unicode CIDs. Glyphs must exist in the selected face; Liberation Sans alone still shows `?` for CJK.

sections.heading: Arabic and Hebrew: OT shaping via go-text/typesetting
sections.body: OpenType shaping runs through the allowlisted pure-Go module `github.com/go-text/typesetting` (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) when the active face has a GSUB table. `TextShow` / `ShapeTextFont` drive the pure-Go HarfBuzz port, then reverse-cmap shaped glyphs to Unicode CIDs for Type0 Identity-H.
bullets: OT joining and ligation (e.g. Lam-Alef) apply when GSUB is present and the reverse-cmap covers the glyphs.
Fallback with no face, no GSUB, or unmapped glyphs: RTL run reverse plus best-effort presentation-form joining in `ShapeText`.
Faces with neither Presentation Forms nor a usable GSUB reverse-cmap will still look disconnected.
Real CGO HarfBuzz is rejected; `TestDirectModuleAllowlist` pins the module list.

sections.heading: CJK needs a capable face
sections.body: CJK (Han, kana, Hangul) works when a capable TTF is on the font path; Hangul specifically needs `fonts-noto-cjk` or any Hangul-capable TTF on `--font-path`. `writing-mode: vertical-rl|lr` is parsed but lays out as a horizontal block. In mixed Latin + CJK runs, Latin glyphs missing from the CJK face are drawn with embedded Liberation while CJK continues on the Type0 sibling of the original face.

sections.heading: Indic and other complex scripts: partial
sections.body: OpenType applies when the face and reverse-cmap succeed, but production Indic quality is not claimed beyond that. The fallback keeps combining marks after the base with no in-tree matra reordering.

sections.heading: @font-face: TTF / OTF / WOFF1
sections.body: `@font-face` is partial: `url(...ttf|otf|woff)` sources are fetched through the document's loader (local paths under `--allow-local-files` / `--allow`, remote `http(s)` under the same NetworkPolicy as `img` / `link`), parsed (WOFF1 decompressed to SFNT via `compress/zlib`, TrueType outlines only), and registered for the document on both PDF and image paths (`prepare.ResourceContext.MergeFontFaces`).
bullets: WOFF1 is supported: decompress, then `pdf.ParseTTF`, TrueType outlines only.
`.woff2`, `.eot`, and `data:` sources are skipped with a warning (`internal/convert/prepare/styles.go:468-476`); remote `http(s)` sources are fetched, not skipped.
`font-weight` and `font-style` on `@font-face` are parsed but ignored at register time (the alias is the family name only).

`halt` / `palt` are requested via typesetting `FontFeatures` for CJK / East-Asian punctuation runs, and via `ParseFontFeatureSettings` / `ShapeTextFontWithFeatures` when CSS `font-feature-settings` is supplied. CSS `font-feature-settings`, `font-kerning`, and `font-variant-caps` wiring is in-flight 0.2.6 work on master (CHANGELOG 0.2.6, plans/0.2.6/), not in the cut 0.2.5 release.

content.title: Rejected and skipped formats
content.body: CFF / `OTTO` OpenType fonts are rejected outright: TrueType outlines only (`pdf.ParseTTF` returns `errFontCFFNotSupported`). WOFF2 is not supported: `pdf.ParseFontBytes` returns `errWOFF2Unsupported` because Brotli is not allowlisted, and the gap is pinned by `TestDecodeWOFF2Gap` (internal/pdf/woff_test.go:210). `.eot` and `data:` `@font-face` sources are skipped with a warning; remote `http(s)` sources are fetched under the same ACL and NetworkPolicy as other subresources.
